mode: Detailed 3D only; white models have no solar joints or tracking callback

sources.document: NASA RP-1357 Mir Hardware Heritage, Part 2
findings: Almaz/Salyut 2, 3, 5: arrays could track Sun in most station attitudes.
Salyut 6: three driven arrays with Sun sensors and rotating connections.

sources.document: Space station propulsion requirements study, NASA-CR-178542
sources.finding: Skylab solar-inertial orientation provided solar tracking without array articulation.

sources.document: NASA TM-106940, Analysis of shadowing effects on MIR photovoltaic and solar dynamic power systems
findings: Mir base: two one-axis wings and one stationary wing.
Kvant-1 and Kvant-2 use one-axis tracking.
Predicted 1995 configuration does not document the complete later Spektr configuration.
Spektr had three undamaged arrays after the 25 June 1997 collision.
Gimbal/Sun-tracking control failures and partial restoration were reported. This supports steerable Spektr wings; it is not a complete motor telemetry archive.

sources.finding: Spektr arrived with two pairs of solar arrays.

limitations: Single-axis hinges calibrated to existing model geometry. Deployed source pose preserved at zero angle.
Nominal +/-90-degree sweep is an implementation assumption, not surveyed historical end stops.
Sun direction and orbital reference calculated at consulted date. Historical motor angles, wheel speeds, eclipse parking, faults and exact station attitudes are not available.
Whole-station Sun-pointing for realistic Salyut 1 and Skylab is a nominal operating mode, not a dated reconstruction of every maneuver.
Mir source configuration remains the selected original Celestia asset; no physical-hardware/date configuration changes introduced.
